stem: Riya sets up a double slit with a red laser in her college lab. Keeping the laser and screen fixed, she swaps in slits that are half as far apart. What happens to the fringes?

options.C: Same width, but brighter, because closer slits make extra light energy
options.D: Same width; only the colour of the fringes changes

r1.text: Slits closer means the whole pattern squeezes, so the fringes get thinner.

r2.text: Fringe width is lambda D by d, so if d is halved the width doubles.

r3.text: When the slits are closer the beams overlap more and interference makes more light.

stem: In his school lab, Arjun uses a 600 nm laser, a screen 1.5 m away and slits 0.30 mm apart, getting 3.0 mm fringes. He swaps in slits 0.15 mm apart, keeping everything else same. New fringe width?

options.D: 3.0 mm, but the bright fringes get brighter because closer slits make extra light

r1.text: Beta equals lambda D over d, and d got halved, so beta doubles to 6 mm.

r2.text: Half the slit gap means half the fringe gap, so 1.5 mm.

r3.text: Width won't change, the interference just puts more energy into the bright bands.

verify_flags: SLIP option B (0.60 mm) is a power-of-ten slip on 6.0 mm

stem: At a science fair in Pune, Kabir's double-slit fringes are too thin to see clearly. Without changing the laser or moving the screen, what should he do to make the fringes wider?

options.A: Use slits that are farther apart
options.B: Cover one slit, so the half pattern left spreads out wider
options.C: Use a stronger laser so interference adds more light to each fringe
options.D: Use slits that are closer together

r1.text: If one slit is blocked you only get half the fringes, so they have more room.

r2.text: Slits farther apart spread everything out, so the fringes get wider too.

r3.text: Fringe width goes as 1 by d, so a smaller slit gap gives wider fringes.

verify_flags: Assumes slit width and wavelength unchanged; a stronger laser changes brightness only, not fringe width

stem: During a power cut, Meera shines a battery laser through a double slit in her Chennai hostel and sees clear fringes on the wall. Her friend sticks tape over one slit. What does the wall show now?

options.A: The fringes vanish; a broad, dimmer patch of light from the open slit remains
options.B: Only the half of the fringe pattern on the open slit's side remains
options.C: The wall goes almost dark, since the light was being produced by the two beams interfering
options.D: Every second bright fringe disappears, leaving half the fringes

r1.text: The bright light came from interference, so without it there is hardly any light.

r2.text: Fringes need waves from both slits to meet, so with one slit there are no fringes, just its own spread-out light.

r3.text: Each slit makes its own share of fringes, so one slit leaves half of them.

verify_flags: Open slit gives its single-slit diffraction pattern: broad central band, centre intensity I0 instead of 4I0; looks uniform-ish only if slit is narrow
